name: Trufend – Security, Malware Scanner & Firewall
author: shewa

sections.description:
A Simpler Approach to WordPress Security

Popular WordPress security plugins such as Wordfence Security, All-In-One Security (AIOS), Solid Security, Sucuri Security, and WP Cerber offer a wide range of security features and protection options.

While comprehensive security solutions are valuable, not every website owner needs a complicated security configuration or an extensive collection of security tools.

Trufend takes a simpler, more focused approach to WordPress security.

Instead of overwhelming you with complex settings, Trufend brings essential security features together in one straightforward dashboard. Its modular design lets you enable only the protection features your website needs.

Why consider Trufend?

  • Simple Dashboard: Manage essential WordPress security features from one place without navigating through complicated settings.
  • Modular Security: Enable or disable individual security modules according to your website’s requirements.
  • Focused Protection: Get practical tools for login security, brute force protection, malware scanning, security hardening, activity monitoring, and backups.
  • Privacy-conscious: Your website data stays within your WordPress installation by default, without sending site data to external services.
  • Developer-friendly: A straightforward security toolkit for WordPress developers, freelancers, agencies, and website owners.
  • No Unnecessary Complexity: Focus on the security controls you actually need instead of configuring features you may never use.

Looking for a straightforward WordPress security plugin?

If you want practical WordPress security features without an unnecessarily complicated setup, give Trufend a try.

Trufend offers a focused and modular alternative for website owners who prefer simplicity and control over their WordPress security configuration.

WordPress Security Features

Trufend includes the following security modules:

  • IP Lock (Brute Force Protection) — Protect your WordPress login page against brute force attacks. Limit failed login attempts, automatically block abusive IP addresses, and manage blocked IPs from the settings page.
  • Login Security — Strengthen WordPress login security by hiding login error hints, configuring an optional custom login URL, and enabling email-based two-factor authentication (2FA).
  • Admin User Protection — Enforce stronger administrator passwords and surface important account changes to improve administrator account security.
  • Security Headers — Improve browser-level security by sending common HTTP security headers, including X-Frame-Options and Referrer-Policy.
  • XML-RPC Protection — Disable WordPress XML-RPC functionality when it is not needed to reduce unnecessary attack surfaces.
  • User Enumeration Protection — Block common author-scanning techniques that attackers use to discover WordPress usernames.
  • REST API Protection — Restrict anonymous access to WordPress REST API endpoints when configured, helping protect information that should not be publicly accessible.
  • Comment Protection — Add a lightweight honeypot to WordPress comment forms to help reduce automated spam submissions.
  • User Activity Log — Monitor and review recent security-related activity directly from your WordPress dashboard.
  • WordPress Malware Scanner — Scan individual PHP files for suspicious code patterns commonly associated with malware, obfuscated code, backdoors, and malicious scripts. Review flagged files to investigate potential security issues.
  • WordPress Backups — Create manual database or website file backups using background processing. Keep backup archives available for additional recovery options.
  • File Permissions Manager — Browse WordPress files and directories and review their permissions directly from the WordPress admin dashboard.

Why Choose Trufend?

  • All-in-one WordPress Security: Manage multiple website security features from one dashboard.
  • Modular Security Controls: Enable only the security modules your website needs.
  • Simple Configuration: Manage essential WordPress security settings without complicated configurations.
  • Privacy-conscious: Trufend does not send website data to external services by default.
  • Developer-friendly: Practical security controls for WordPress developers, freelancers, agencies, and website owners.
  • Multisite Support: Manage security settings across WordPress Multisite installations.

Is Trufend a WordPress Firewall?

Trufend provides application-level WordPress security and hardening features to help protect against common attacks. It is not a replacement for a network-level firewall, server security, or a dedicated Web Application Firewall (WAF).

For stronger protection, use Trufend alongside secure hosting, regular WordPress updates, and a reputable WAF service.

Privacy and Data Protection

Trufend is designed with privacy in mind. It does not send website data to external services by default. Security management and activity monitoring are handled within your WordPress installation.

External Libraries

Trufend bundles the following library with its distribution:

  • shewa/wp-job-queue — GPL-2.0-or-later — Background job processing for scans and backups.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/trufend, or install Trufend through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Open Trufend in the WordPress admin menu to review the security dashboard and enable the modules you need.

If you install from source, run composer install --no-dev in the plugin directory before activation so bundled dependencies are available.
sections.faq:
Is Trufend a free WordPress security plugin?

Yes. Trufend provides multiple WordPress security features, including brute force protection, login security, malware scanning, security headers, activity monitoring, and backups.

Does Trufend phone home or collect analytics?

No. Trufend does not send site data to external services by default. Optional Pro upgrade links can be changed with the trufend_pro_upgrade_url filter.

How does Trufend protect against brute force attacks?

Trufend’s IP Lock module tracks failed login attempts per IP address. Once an IP exceeds the configured threshold, it is blocked and redirected away from the login page.

You can manage blocked IP addresses from the Trufend → IP Lock settings page.

How do I unblock my IP if I get locked out?

If you lock yourself out, you can unblock your own IP directly from the Trufend → IP Lock settings page while logged in from a different IP.

Alternatively, temporarily deactivate the plugin through FTP or cPanel and reactivate it after adjusting the login attempt threshold.

Does Trufend support two-factor authentication (2FA)?

Yes. Trufend’s Login Security module includes email-based two-factor authentication to add an additional verification step to the WordPress login process.

What does the WordPress Malware Scanner check for?

The scanner inspects PHP files inside your WordPress installation for suspicious patterns commonly found in malware, including obfuscated eval(base64_decode(...)) calls, hidden backdoors, and injected redirect scripts.

It flags files that match known suspicious patterns so you can review and investigate them.

The scanner uses file-pattern detection. It is not a real-time malware scanner or firewall, so it works best as a periodic security check alongside regular backups and other security measures.

Does Trufend include a WordPress firewall?

Trufend provides application-level security and WordPress hardening features, including login protection, XML-RPC protection, user enumeration protection, and security headers.

It is not a full Web Application Firewall (WAF) and does not replace server-level or network-level firewall protection. For defense in depth, combine Trufend with secure hosting and a reputable WAF service, such as Cloudflare.

Does Trufend provide automatic backups?

Trufend allows you to create manual database or website file backups using background processing. The backup functionality does not imply automatic scheduled backups.

Can I use Trufend on WordPress Multisite?

Yes. When network-activated, settings can be managed network-wide and per-site tables are cleaned up on uninstall.

Does Trufend modify wp-config.php?

Only when Pro is active and you enable the file editor protection toggle. Trufend adds a managed DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT constant and removes it on uninstall when possible.

Will uninstalling Trufend remove my data?

Yes. When you delete the plugin, Trufend removes its database tables, settings, scheduled events, and stored backup archives by default.

Use the trufend_uninstall_delete_backups filter if you want to keep backup files.
